scope: Eight written statement/proof pairs: identifiability, memory, composition, simulation, symmetry, governance quotient/refinement, and institutional language transport.
provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review.

cards.label: prop:identifiability
cards.title: Behavior alone does not identify implementation
cards.hypotheses: The two realizations have the same law of the complete transcript available under each permitted evaluation experiment. The decision uses that transcript and a common randomization rule. The accuracy bound uses equal priors.
cards.decisive_argument: A common decision kernel sends equal transcript laws to equal decision laws. If q is the probability of choosing the first realization, binary accuracy is (q + 1 - q)/2 = 1/2. Abstention cannot increase unconditional accuracy.
cards.dependency_graph: Equal transcript laws + common decision kernel → equal output laws → equal-prior accuracy bound. All leaves are explicit assumptions or the direct argument.
cards.boundary_cases: Identical deterministic transcripts, randomized decisions, and constant decisions. If tests are adaptive, their complete available transcript law must satisfy the premise; equality of isolated test marginals alone is insufficient. Unequal priors and extra implementation-dependent side information are outside the accuracy claim.
cards.next_check: For an application, enumerate the evaluator’s available observations and show equality for its complete experiment.
cards.provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review

cards.label: prop:memory
cards.title: Exact finite-memory lower bound
cards.hypotheses: Histories are equivalent when they require identical output sequences for every permitted continuation. N counts their equivalence classes. The quotient construction additionally assumes prefix closure and a transition congruence on the admissible history domain.
cards.decisive_argument: Two inequivalent histories cannot receive the same exact deterministic summary: a distinguishing continuation would require different outputs from the same summary. Thus the summary has at least N states. For positive finite N, B fixed-length bits offer at most 2^B states, so B is at least ceil(log2 N). A transition congruence makes the next class independent of the representative.
cards.dependency_graph: Continuation distinguishability → no collision between inequivalent histories → state-count lower bound. Add 1 ≤ N < ∞ → ordinary numerical bit bound. Add transition congruence and the declared continuation closure → well-defined quotient updates.
cards.boundary_cases: N = 1 gives zero required bits; powers of two and their successors explain the ceiling. For an empty history family, N = 0 and the displayed ordinary logarithm is undefined. Infinite index admits no finite exact summary, rather than a finite numerical logarithm bound. The introduction’s finite-domain convention supports the intended finite reading, but the local history-family definition does not explicitly state positive finite index.
cards.remaining_gap: Make the positive finite-index restriction explicit in the source statement before counting this as an unqualified pass. This is a domain-clarity finding, not a counterexample to the intended finite-state argument.
cards.next_check: In a future source edition, specify a nonempty admissible history domain with 1 ≤ N < ∞ for the numerical bound, and state that allowed updates remain in the domain of the transition congruence. Keep the general no-collision statement separate.
cards.verdict: correct only after a stated restriction
cards.provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review

obligations.proof_implications: passed for the stated finite restriction

cards.label: prop:composition
cards.title: Compositional one-step closure
cards.hypotheses: Surjections X → Z → W and transition kernels use the same control family. The two per-state, per-control total-variation errors are uniformly bounded by epsilon_1 and epsilon_2 as defined immediately before the proposition.
cards.decisive_argument: Insert the pushforward of the intermediate kernel. The triangle inequality bounds the second discrepancy by epsilon_2. For the first, summing signed masses within each fibre and applying the triangle inequality shows that deterministic pushforward cannot increase half the l1 distance. This yields epsilon_1 + epsilon_2; induction adds the errors across L levels.
cards.dependency_graph: Finite probability laws → grouped-sum triangle inequality → pushforward nonexpansiveness; combine with the two uniform bounds → two-level estimate → finite induction.
cards.boundary_cases: Identity and constant maps, zero errors, L = 1, and sums exceeding one. A bound greater than one is loose but valid. The separate finite-horizon corollary also needs prop:time, which is not newly audited here. Causal intervention compatibility is not implied.
cards.next_check: Audit prop:time and its control assumptions before extending this review to the adjacent finite-horizon corollary.
cards.provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review

cards.label: prop:flatten
cards.title: Simulation by an unrestricted controller
cards.hypotheses: The hierarchy is finite and effectively specified, its components are computable, and the controller stores component states, messages, and scheduling variables. It executes the same transitions in the same order, with the same input and random-tape consumption.
cards.decisive_argument: Initialize matching records. One scheduled local transition reads identical records and random choices and therefore produces identical successor records and external outputs. Induction preserves equality along every finite execution prefix.
cards.dependency_graph: Effective representation and matching initialization → identical scheduled update → record equality invariant → identical external transcript.
cards.boundary_cases: A single component, an empty transcript, inactive components, and randomized components coupled by the same tape. The scheduler and random-consumption convention belong to the simulated specification. No time, memory, communication, or decentralized-access bound is asserted.
cards.next_check: Any claimed architectural advantage must specify the resource or information restrictions on the comparison controller.
cards.provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review

cards.label: prop:symmetry
cards.title: Symmetry lock for identical deterministic agents
cards.hypotheses: The deterministic joint transition is equivariant for permutations of agent labels. The initial joint state and every supplied input are invariant under that action.
cards.decisive_argument: Writing the input explicitly, equivariance gives gF(X,u) = F(gX,gu). With gX = X and gu = u, the next state is fixed by every permutation. Induct from the invariant initial state.
cards.dependency_graph: Equivariance + invariant state and input → invariant successor → induction in time.
cards.boundary_cases: Zero updates, one agent, and invariant auxiliary state. Distinct addresses, unequal observations, or asymmetric scheduling can break the input/state hypothesis. The proposition concerns deterministic trajectories, not merely a symmetric distribution of random trajectories.
cards.next_check: For a concrete architecture, include scheduler state, addresses, and observations when checking invariance.
cards.provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review

cards.label: thm:govquot
cards.title: Exact governance quotient
cards.hypotheses: S is finite and nonempty; the action vocabulary is finite with fixed meanings; the state map is surjective. The preceding definition makes each partial transition defined exactly on its enabled action set.
cards.decisive_argument: Factorization forces equal labels, enabled sets, and successor fibres. Conversely these conditions define representative-independent quotient labels, enabled sets, and successors. Surjectivity supplies each quotient value and forces uniqueness on the declared enabled domain. Equal enabled sets and preserved successor fibres then give equal legal action and label sequences by induction.
cards.dependency_graph: Fibre conditions ↔ well-defined quotient data; surjectivity → uniqueness; enabled-set equality + successor compatibility → finite-trace induction.
cards.boundary_cases: Deadlocked states, an empty action vocabulary, a singleton state space, and the empty action sequence. Quotient transitions use the same partial-map convention: they are defined exactly for quotient-enabled actions. Treating them as arbitrary extensions outside that domain would not be the stated governance structure.
cards.next_check: Verify the fibre conditions for a proposed concrete institutional summary; existence of a useful nontrivial quotient is not automatic.
cards.provenance: AI-assisted sequential self-review; not independent peer review

cards.label: prop:govrefine
cards.title: Coarsest finite governance summary
cards.hypotheses: Start with blocks sharing the same institutional labels and enabled sets, then refine by the blocks of every enabled successor. The finite state/action model and transition convention are those of thm:govquot.
cards.decisive_argument: Each strict refinement increases the block count, which is at most |S|. At stabilization the quotient conditions hold. Any compatible partition refines the initial partition and, inductively, every refinement. It therefore refines the stable partition, which is itself compatible and has the least number of blocks.
cards.dependency_graph: Finite block count → termination bound; fixed point → thm:govquot (audited in this batch); induction over competing compatible partitions → coarseness → minimum size.
cards.boundary_cases: An initially discrete partition takes zero strict refinements; all-deadlock blocks need only distinguish labels. The bound counts strict refinements, not the final equality test or runtime. Equal enabled sets within a block make the successor comparisons well-typed.
cards.next_check: If actions or protected labels change, recompute the initial partition and refinement; minimality is relative to the fixed contract.

cards.label: prop:languagetrace
cards.title: Preservation of finite institutional conversations
cards.hypotheses: Definition def:language supplies equivalent admission/rejection, commuting admitted transitions, and common event records on a transition-closed declared domain. Message translation depends on the evolving source state. Composition uses matching intermediate institutions and domains.
cards.decisive_argument: Equivalent definedness gives the same first rejection point. For an admitted step, transition commutation preserves the state relation and event equality preserves the record. Induction handles every finite admitted prefix. For composition, compose state maps, substitute the two transition identities, and apply the two definedness equivalences and transitivity of event equality.
cards.dependency_graph: The three defining equalities/definedness conditions → one-step preservation → prefix induction. Well-typed composition of two such transports → the same three conditions for the composite.
cards.boundary_cases: Empty conversation, rejection of the first message, and rejection after a nonempty admitted prefix. No translation after an undefined source successor is needed. Composition is on the shared declared domain: if restricted domains are used, the first state translator must land in the second’s faithful domain, or the composite must be restricted accordingly. Surjectivity and preservation of unrelated target messages are not claimed.
cards.next_check: For an implementation, exhibit the compatible domains and access to the state needed to compute the context-dependent message translation.

decisions.reason: Seven additional implications pass targeted self-review; the finite-memory bit bound needs an explicit positive finite-index restriction. Combined coverage is 26 of 62, including one qualified verdict; 36 remain unreviewed.
